risks: No direct risk to participants; the risk is a triage rule built on overstated or double-counted evidence that falsely reassures or crowds the resuscitation area.
data: Extraction forms, the citation matrix and confidence ratings are kept on the department's shared drive and published with the report.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: older adults, people on beta blockers, and people with darker skin or poor peripheral perfusion (in whom capillary sampling may be harder) may be falsely reassured more often; findings by age, medication and sample type are extracted and reported, and the absence of such data is stated.
effectiveness: The review is useful if it tells the sepsis group what a normal and a raised lactate can and cannot justify at triage.
efficiency: Uses existing reviews rather than new primary data; fits the fellow's time.
costs: Staff time within existing roles; no translation budget.
partnerships: The sepsis group, triage nurses, the resuscitation team lead, the librarian, and two patient partners who survived sepsis.
rebPath: No ethics review needed for a review of published literature (research office reference RO-2026-0907, 2026-09-11); the protocol will be registered in a public register of review protocols before screening.
limitations: Depends on the quality and reporting of the reviews; language restriction; predictive values depend on an estimated local prevalence.
summary: No participant risk; equity reporting by age, medication and sample type; protocol registration before screening.
